title: Builders and ported tests
bridge: A builder is like a Playwright page object that sets up state through the real UI instead of writing to the database. Except: here the "UI" is the cloud's API called in-process. Each builder returns the ids a test needs, after the serializers and permission checks ran for real.
intro: With the fakes in place, tests need data: sites, projects, schemas, datasets and code objects. This lesson builds that data through the API with the integration tests' own client. Then it ports 15 cloud-only tests off shared QA. It stays Python: the tests run inside fcp's Django backend.

picture.caption: A ported test keeps its own calls; only the transport and the data source change.

steps.text: calls create_project(), add_collaborator() as on QA
APIClient.generic() runs the request with a real JWT
an import schedules a task; the builder finishes it with complete_task()
the QA copy runs nightly for 2 green weeks, then is deleted

sections.h: Data through the API, not through factories
p: factory_boy writes rows straight into the database. That is fine for a model test, but it skips the serializers, the permission checks and the import status changes. An endpoint test that starts from factory rows can pass while the real flow fails. So tests_api builds its data the way the UI and the SDK do: through the API.

The integration tests already have a client for that. rhinoCore/integration-tests/integration_test_utils/common.py defines RhinoAPI, whose make_call() sends HTTP with requests.request. rhino_api_wrapper.py wraps it as RhinoAPITestWrapper with methods like create_project(). If tests_api reuses that wrapper, ported tests keep their own calls almost unchanged.

To reuse it, G7-06 first adds a seam to RhinoAPI. The two requests.request(...) calls in make_call, including the page fetches, move into one _send() method. Runs against QA behave exactly as before. A subclass can now override _send().

callout.text: Fake data only. Names and emails come from Faker, passwords are generated per test, and import outputs are fake rows. Never copy rows from QA or prod; PHI never enters a test.

p: The new class lives in tests_api/api.py. It subclasses RhinoAPI and swaps the transport: DRF's APIClient instead of the network (lesson p10-3). Authentication stays real: the token comes from the auth/obtain_token endpoint, so the login path is tested too.
sections.because: We fetch a real JWT instead of force_authenticate, because a ported test should prove that login and permissions work, not skip them.

code.text:
import json
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from rest_framework.test import APIClient

from integration_test_utils.common import RhinoAPI
from integration_test_utils.rhino_api_wrapper import RhinoAPITestWrapper


class InProcessRhinoAPI(RhinoAPI):
    """The integration tests' RhinoAPI with the HTTP call swapped for DRF's APIClient: same auth (a real JWT from
    auth/obtain_token), same error handling and pagination, but no network and no shared QA."""

    def __init__(self, user_username: str, user_password: str, api_version: str = "v2"):
        super().__init__(api_version=api_version, user_username=user_username, user_password=user_password)
        self.api_base_url = "/api/"
        self.client = APIClient()

    def _request_jwt_token(self) -> str:
        credentials = {"email": self.user_username, "password": self.user_password}
        return self.client.post(f"{self.api_base_versioned_url}auth/obtain_token", credentials).json()["access"]

To turn query parameters into a query string.
DRF's in-process test client: no server, no network.
The integration tests' client. pythonpath in tests_api/pytest.ini includes ../rhinoCore/integration-tests, so this import works.
The wrapper with the high-level calls (create_project and friends).
Same behaviour as RhinoAPI (errors, pagination, token cache), different transport.
Takes the user's email and password, like the parent.
Let the parent set version, user and trace id.
A path, not a host. api_base_versioned_url is a property built from it, so every URL becomes /api/v2/...
One in-process client per user.
Override the parent's token request, which uses requests.post.
The same form fields the parent sends.
Post them to the real endpoint and return the access token from the JSON.

p: _send() receives what make_call would have given requests.request and replays it through APIClient.generic(). Django's test client takes headers as META keys: Authorization becomes HTTP_AUTHORIZATION, X-Trace-Id becomes HTTP_X_TRACE_ID.

Two fixtures complete the ticket. builder.site() posts test/create_test_data with TestDataCreator's "custom" scenario: a workgroup, a user with a $var password and a user_role. It returns a Site with a logged-in wrapper.

api_client is a wrapper on the in-process transport for the site's workgroup. It has the same name as the integration fixture, so ported tests keep working. Only the bootstrap Rhino admin comes from RhinoAdminTestFactory.
sections.because: We convert headers to META keys and encode the body ourselves, because APIClient.generic() takes raw Django request parts, not requests-style arguments.

notes.text: The new seam. make_call (and its page fetches) call it instead of requests.request().
Each header becomes HTTP_<NAME> with dashes turned into underscores; empty values are skipped.
A JSON body is encoded here; otherwise the raw data. Multipart uploads need a check per endpoint.
Run any HTTP method through the whole Django stack in-process.
The query parameters, encoded, plus the headers as META entries.
A factory function the api_client fixture uses.
The normal wrapper, logged in as this user, with this workgroup as default.
Swap its transport for the in-process one. Every wrapper method now runs without a network.
The test gets the same object type as on QA.

p: G7-08 adds builders for the next layer of data: data schemas, datasets and code objects. Most cloud-only scenarios need a project with a schema, a dataset and a code object. Building them through the API catches what factories skip: serializer validation, permission checks and import status changes.
The file starts with a dataclass (lesson p10-1) that holds everything a test needs about one site.
sections.because: We return a small Site record, because every later builder needs the site's logged-in client and its workgroup.

code.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from faker import Faker

from fcp_common.rhinoTaskServices.task_common import TaskStatus, TaskType
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.models.dataset import Dataset

from integration_test_utils.rhino_api_wrapper import RhinoAPITestWrapper

SCHEMA_CSVS = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "rhinoCore" / "integration-tests" / "pytest_fixtures"
fake = Faker()


@dataclass
class Site:
    api: RhinoAPITestWrapper  # logged in as the site's user, on the in-process transport (see builder.site())
    workgroup_uid: str
    email: str
    password: str  # generated per test; fake

p: data_schema() calls the wrapper's create_schema with a CSV. dataset() is the interesting one. It imports through POST datasets/ as the UI does, then lets the fake client answer the import task.

It needs a new parameter. RhinoAPITestWrapper.create_dataset hard-codes "sync": True today; add a sync parameter. A sync import polls the database in the request thread while it waits, so the fake could never answer. code_object() (not shown) posts to code_objects/ with TestDataCreator's python_code config. The helpers pneumonia(site) and python_code(site, project_uid) return small dataclasses of uids.
sections.because: We import with sync=False and finish the task from the test, because the fake answers only when the test calls complete_task().

code.text:
def data_schema(site: Site, project_uid: str, csv_name: str = "Pneumonia Input Schema.csv") -> str:
    return site.api.create_schema(project_uid, SCHEMA_CSVS / csv_name)


def dataset(site: Site, project_uid: str, schema_uid: str, onprem_client, import_output: dict) -> str:
    """Import through POST datasets/ like the UI does; the fake client "runs" the import task.
    sync=False on purpose: a sync import polls the DB in this thread while waiting, so the fake could never answer."""
    created = site.api.create_dataset(fake.catch_phrase(), project_uid, schema_uid, "/rhino_data/fake.csv", sync=False)
    task = next(t for t in reversed(onprem_client.scheduled) if t.task_type == TaskType.DATASET_IMPORT)
    onprem_client.complete_task(task.task_uid, TaskStatus.COMPLETED, import_output)  # fake rows, made with Faker
    status = site.api.api.make_call("GET", f"datasets/{created['uid']}/")["data"]["import_status"]
    assert status == Dataset.ImportStatusTypes.COMPLETE, status
    return created["uid"]

sections.h: Porting, part 1: same calls, no QA (G7-18)
p: G7-18 moves 8 tests that only need the cloud: permission/test_project_permission.py (4), test_client_offline_validation.py (2), test_tensorboard.py::test_get_or_create_tensorboard_no_logs_returns_guidance and test_runtime_file.py::test_cross_workgroup_access. They wait in the QA queue today although they never need a real client.

Move, don't copy. The QA original gets @pytest.mark.nightly, which per-push QA runs skip. Once the port has been green in CI for 2 weeks, delete the original. Assert on what the caller sees (status codes, error text, fields, row counts), never on which internal calls happened.
sections.because: We keep the original calls line for line, so a reviewer can compare the port and the QA test at a glance.

code.text:
"""Ported from rhinoCore/integration-tests/permission/test_project_permission.py: the same calls, run in-process
against the fakes instead of qa-cloud. The QA original is marked nightly until this has been green for 2 weeks."""

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.services.permission_service import remove_rhino_admin_from_permissions
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.services.project_permission.permission_constants import ActionTypes, PermissionPersona


def test_project_permission_endpoint(api_client):
    project_uid = api_client.create_project(permissions=None)
    expected = remove_rhino_admin_from_permissions(ActionTypes().get_project_default_dict())
    assert api_client.get_project_permissions(project_uid) == expected

notes.text: The docstring says where the test came from and when the QA original goes away.

sections.h: Porting, part 2: a builder replaces a QA id
p: The second test needed a second workgroup. On QA it used the hard-coded collaborator workgroup 65e46694-0951-4634-a839-634af42a8177. In tests_api, builder.site() makes a fresh one.

The same goes for the pre-seeded offline workgroup cafecafe-cafe-cafe-cafe-000000000004. Find how the cloud decides a client is offline (RH-5356). Then build that state with the fake's offline_agents or a builder.
The runtime-file test uses the in-memory object store. The TensorBoard test uses the fake's empty GetTensorBoardLogsMetadata.
sections.because: We build the collaborator with builder.site(), because a hard-coded QA id ties the test to one shared environment.

code.text:
def test_project_collab_permission_endpoint(api_client, builder):
    collaborator = builder.site()  # was the hard-coded QA workgroup 65e46694-0951-4634-a839-634af42a8177
    project_uid = api_client.create_project(permissions=None)
    api_client.add_collaborator(project_uid, collaborator.workgroup_uid)
    permissions = api_client.get_site_permissions(project_uid)[collaborator.workgroup_uid]["permissions"]
    assert permissions == remove_rhino_admin_from_permissions(ActionTypes().get_site_default_dict())

    custom = ActionTypes().get_site_default_dict()
    custom[ActionTypes.SHARE_SECURE_ACCESS_LIST.name] = [
        PermissionPersona.RHINO_ADMIN.name,
        PermissionPersona.COLLABORATOR_MEMBER.name,
    ]
    project_uid = api_client.create_project(permissions=None)
    api_client.add_collaborator(project_uid, collaborator.workgroup_uid, permissions=custom)
    permissions = api_client.get_site_permissions(project_uid)[collaborator.workgroup_uid]["permissions"]
    assert permissions[ActionTypes.SHARE_SECURE_ACCESS_LIST.name] == [PermissionPersona.COLLABORATOR_MEMBER.name]

"""Ported from rhinoCore/integration-tests/test_semantic_mapping.py and test_vocabulary.py (custom vocabularies)."""

from helpers import assert_vocabulary_terms  # moved from test_semantic_mapping.py into tests_api/helpers.py

START_INDEXING = "rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.celery_tasks.vocabulary_indexing.start_indexing"


def test_custom_vocabulary_no_identifier(api_client):
    project_uid = api_client.create_project()
    vocabulary_uid = api_client.create_vocabulary(
        project_uid=project_uid,
        name="test_custom_vocabulary_no_identifier",
        terms="\n".join(f"test_term_name{i}" for i in range(1, 5)),
        type="custom",
    )
    expected = [{"term_display_name": f"test_term_name{i}", "term_identifier": None} for i in range(1, 5)]
    assert_vocabulary_terms(api_client, vocabulary_uid, expected)

sections.h: Porting vocabularies, part 2: queued, not drained
p: The large upload is a multipart upload: the file goes up in parts, which land in the in-memory object store. index_large_vocabulary then queues a Celery chain that starts an indexing VM and OpenSearch. The API layer runs neither, so the test checks the chain was queued and stops there.

test_very_large_vocabulary_upload and the full-flow vocabulary tests stay on the QA nightly, because they need real indexing. After the port, time the whole layer. If it is over 3 minutes locally, look at the 10 slowest tests (--durations=10) before adding more.
sections.because: We assert on task_queue.sent and never drain, because draining would try to start a VM the API layer does not have.

code.text:
def test_large_vocabulary_upload(api_client, task_queue, object_store):
    project_uid = api_client.create_project()
    vocabulary_uid = upload_large_vocabulary(api_client, project_uid)  # same helper and file as the QA test
    assert api_client.get_vocabulary(vocabulary_uid)["status"]  # check: the status the upload sets before indexing
    # index_large_vocabulary queues a Celery chain that starts an indexing VM. Check it was queued, but do not drain
    # it: the API layer runs no VM and no OpenSearch. The QA nightly keeps the full indexing flow.
    assert START_INDEXING in [task.name for task in task_queue.sent]

The QA test's upload steps, moved into tests_api/helpers.py. The sketch leaves out that import; add it.
The vocabulary exists and has a status. Check which status the upload sets before indexing.
Why we stop here: no VM and no OpenSearch in the API layer.
The indexing task was sent. Check whether it is the chain's first task or sits inside the chain option.

quiz.q: Why does InProcessRhinoAPI fetch a real JWT instead of calling force_authenticate?

options.text: Because APIClient cannot authenticate without a token.
options.why: force_authenticate works fine in unit tests; this is a choice.

options.text: Because the ported tests should prove the login path works, not skip it.
options.why: The token comes from auth/obtain_token, so authentication is part of every test.

options.text: Because the QA environment requires it.
options.why: No QA is involved; everything runs in-process.

quiz.q: The dataset builder imports with sync=False. What would happen with sync=True?

options.text: The request thread would poll the database for the result, and the fake could never answer in time.
options.why: The fake answers only when the test calls complete_task(), which cannot happen while the request waits.

options.text: The serializer would reject the request.
options.why: sync=True is valid on QA; the problem is waiting in-process.

quiz.q: A ported test has been green in CI for one week. What happens to the QA original?

options.text: Delete it now; the port works.
options.why: The rule is two green weeks first.

options.text: Keep it running on every push as a backup.
options.why: It is marked nightly, so per-push QA runs skip it.

options.text: It stays, marked @pytest.mark.nightly, until the port has been green for 2 weeks.
options.why: Move, don't copy: the original is deleted after two green weeks.
